findings.description: The generic 'not found' match treats missing beads infrastructure as a nonexistent issue. For an otherwise valid row, a br executable that exits nonzero with 'beads database not found' enters this branch, even though the issue's existence could not be checked.
findings.failure_mode: The validator exits 1 instead of the documented degraded exit 3. Consequently, the new workflow fails CI instead of issuing its intended warning when br is installed but its workspace or database is unavailable.
findings.suggested_fix: Recognize issue absence using the specific ISSUE_NOT_FOUND error code or an equally specific structured response. Classify missing workspace/database errors and other verification failures as unverified.

findings.cross_file_justification: The gate runs in bats-tests.yml on an actions/checkout clone, which is depth-1 unless fetch-depth: 0 is set. In a depth-1 clone every line of every file is blamed on HEAD, which git marks as a boundary commit, so the relaxed branch at line 127 is the ONLY rule CI ever applies.
findings.description: The shallow-boundary relaxation (`expiry <= boundary_date + 30`, lines 127-131 and 199-200) dates the row by the AUTHOR time of the boundary commit. In a depth-1 checkout the boundary commit is HEAD, whose author date has nothing to do with the row and is preserved across rebase-merge, cherry-pick and `git commit --amend`. Two consequences: (a) false failure on main: existing valid row with expiry = today+27, a PR rebase-merged (or an old fix cherry-picked) whose tip commit was authored 35 days ago -> boundary_date = today-35, want = today-5, `expiry > want` -> 'expiry ... is later than the shallow-clone boundary date' -> exit 1, main is red for a row nobody touched. (b) the documented '+30 from the quarantine date' invariant (header lines 22-26) is never enforced in CI for merge-commit pushes: the boundary is the fresh merge commit (date = today), so the effective rule degrades to `today <= expiry <= today+30`; a row written 29 days ago with expiry today+30 passes every CI run.
findings.failure_mode: CI gate exits 1 on push of any commit with an author date more than 30 days old while an unexpired row exists; conversely the +30 rule is unenforceable on the runner so stale rows pass indefinitely as long as expiry <= today+30.
findings.suggested_fix: For the boundary case use `committer-time` (reset by rebase/squash/cherry-pick, always >= author-time) or simply compare against `TODAY + 30`, since the boundary's date carries no information about the row. Alternatively set `fetch-depth: 0` (or `git fetch --unshallow`) in the bats-tests.yml checkout so the exact rule actually runs in CI, and document that the shallow branch is a fallback only.

findings.cross_file_justification: The exact-equality check at lines 197-198 consumes this value.
findings.description: The exact rule (line 197: `expiry != qday + 30` -> problem) converts `author-time` to a UTC calendar date and ignores the `author-tz` line that the same porcelain output provides. An author in UTC-7 committing at 18:00 local on 2026-10-24 produces author-time 2026-10-25T01:00Z; they wrote expiry 2026-11-23 (local date + 30) but the validator wants 2026-11-24 -> exit 1. Same mismatch for anyone who writes the row on day D and commits on D+1, and for every squash-merge (GitHub resets the squash commit's author date to merge time), so on a full clone of main a row authored 2026-10-24 (expiry 2026-11-23) and squash-merged 2026-10-27 fails with 'must be the quarantine date 2026-10-27 + 30 days = 2026-11-26'.
findings.failure_mode: Valid rows fail validation in any full-depth clone (local runs, fetch-depth: 0 CI) whenever author local date != UTC date or whenever the merge strategy rewrites author dates; developers must iterate on the expiry value to satisfy the validator.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the `author-tz` offset when deriving `qday` (porcelain gives `author-tz +0900`), or relax exact equality to a one-day tolerance band `qday+30 <= expiry <= qday+31`, or anchor the rule to the committer date which GitHub sets consistently. Document which one so authors can compute it.

findings.description: `IFS=$'\t' read -r id owner expiry bead reason <<< "$line"` treats TAB as IFS whitespace, so consecutive tabs collapse and leading/trailing tabs are dropped. The column count at line 150 passes (4 tabs) but fields shift. Input `tests/unit/x.bats::t<TAB><TAB>2026-11-23<TAB>bd-abc<TAB>why` (empty owner) yields owner=2026-11-23, expiry=bd-abc, bead=why, reason='' and reports 'expiry "bd-abc" is not an ISO date', 'bead "why" is not a bead id', 'reason is empty' and never 'owner is empty'. Still exits 1 (fail-closed) but the diagnostics point at the wrong columns, and the dedicated `owner is empty` check at line 181 is unreachable for this input.
findings.failure_mode: Misleading error output for any row with an empty middle column; author fixes the wrong field.
findings.suggested_fix: Split on a non-whitespace separator: `IFS=$'\x1f' read -r id owner expiry bead reason <<< "${line//$'\t'/$'\x1f'}"` (US is not IFS whitespace so empty fields survive), or parse with `awk -F'\t'`.

findings.description: Three fragilities in the bead check answer reviewer Q8 ('.beads/ present but br broken -> exit 1 instead of 3'): (1) line 215 captures stdout+stderr together and line 217 feeds the blend to `jq -r '.[0].status'`; any warning line from `br` (schema upgrade, deprecation) makes jq fail -> 'unparseable br show output' -> exit 1, not 3. If `br show --json` emits an object rather than an array, `.[0]` errors the same way for every row. (2) line 223 classifies any failure whose text matches `not found` (case-insensitive) as 'bead not found' -> exit 1; a `br` that is installed but has no workspace and prints e.g. 'beads directory not found' or a wrapper printing 'br: command not found' converts the intended exit-3 degraded path into a hard CI failure. (3) `"$BR" show` inherits the while-loop's stdin (the `tail` process substitution); a CLI that reads stdin would silently consume remaining rows.
findings.failure_mode: Exit 1 (CI red) where the spec says exit 3 (warning), or silently unvalidated rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture stdout and stderr separately (`bout=$(... 2>"$errf")`), match only an explicit code (`ISSUE_NOT_FOUND`) or check `[ -d "$REPO/.beads" ]` before treating anything as 'not found', tolerate object-or-array (`jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0].status else .status end'`), and append `</dev/null` to the `br` call.

findings.cross_file_justification: The totals step (bats-tests.yml line 238) runs under `if: always()` and only fails on rc 1/2; the script's TAP branch never returns non-zero for an unparseable or empty TAP.
findings.description: Answers reviewer Q13: on a TAP parse failure the totals step silently prints zeros. `grep -Ec ... || true` yields 0 for a file with no `ok`/`not ok` lines (e.g. bats aborted before emitting the plan, a formatter change, or a truncated tee), so the step prints `executed=0 skipped=0 quarantined=0` and exits 0. The only other check, `--tap FILE` existence at line 90, passes for an empty file. The `--tap` path is also used to assert the quarantine skip count, so a TAP where the helper's `quarantined:` prefix changes would read as zero quarantined without complaint.
findings.failure_mode: Silent loss of the executed/skipped/quarantined signal the step exists to produce; no failure when the TAP is empty or unparseable.
findings.suggested_fix: After computing `total`, `[[ "$total" -gt 0 ]] || die2 "$TAP: no TAP test lines found"`; optionally cross-check `quarantined` against `rows` and warn on mismatch.

findings.description: `evals/analysis/*/tests` is a shell glob inside a `run:` block that has no `nullglob`. If no directory matches, bash passes the literal string `evals/analysis/*/tests` to pytest, which exits 4 with 'file or directory not found' and fails the step for every push matching the new paths filter. This diff does not add any `evals/analysis/*/tests` directory (the review scope excluded tests), so the dependency is unverified here. Separately, collecting these alongside `tests/security/test_*.py` in one pytest invocation will raise 'import file mismatch' collection errors if two test files share a basename without `__init__.py` packages.
findings.failure_mode: pytest step fails with exit 4 (or collection errors) on every CI run until the directory exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `evals/analysis/<pkg>/tests` is committed in this PR; or guard: `shopt -s nullglob; set -- evals/analysis/*/tests; pytest ... "$@"`. Ensure each tests dir has `__init__.py` or use `--import-mode=importlib`.

findings.cross_file_justification: Script line 89 exits 2 when `$REPO/tests/QUARANTINE.tsv` is missing, and the gate step treats any rc other than 0/3 as a hard error.
findings.description: Answers reviewer Q13 (does a missing tests/QUARANTINE.tsv fail?): yes, exit 2 -> `::error::` -> step exit 2, and the message printed is 'QUARANTINE.tsv invalid or expired', not 'missing'. The TSV and `tests/unit/helpers/quarantine.bash` (sourced at script line 78 under `set -euo pipefail`) are both prerequisites that are not in this diff. If the helper is a bats-only file that references `$BATS_*` at top level, sourcing it fails with exit 1 and the gate reports the same misleading 'invalid or expired' error.
findings.failure_mode: Every CI run on the new paths fails with a misleading annotation if either file is absent or the helper is not plain-bash-sourceable.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify both files ship in this PR and that the helper is sourceable outside bats. Make the gate step distinguish rc 2 ('usage/missing file: see stderr') from rc 1 ('rows invalid or expired').

findings.description: Answers reviewer Q10. The exclusion `^(\./)?[^:]*/(__tests__|tests)/fixtures/[^:]*:` keys on a path segment anywhere, not on the two known fixture roots. `.claude/hooks/tests/fixtures/pre-tool.sh` or `.claude/scripts/tests/fixtures/run.sh` containing a direct `yq '.profile.x'` read is dropped from `hits` and the lint passes. The positive controls in tests/unit/profile-lib.bats plant readers under `.claude/hooks/` directly, so they do not exercise this hole. A smuggled file still needs to be wired into settings/hooks to execute, which bounds the impact, so this is a hardening gap rather than a live exposure.
findings.failure_mode: A profile-key reader under any `*/tests/fixtures/` or `*/__tests__/fixtures/` directory is invisible to the knob-reader lint.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor to the actual fixture roots (e.g. `^(\./)?\.claude/skills/[^/:]+/resources/__tests__/fixtures/` and `^(\./)?tests/fixtures/`) or additionally reject excluded paths that are referenced from `.claude/settings*.json` hooks. Add a negative control in profile-lib.bats that plants a reader under `.claude/hooks/tests/fixtures/` and asserts it is still caught.
